decontamination_notes: Real reference-name validation hardening from GitoxideLabs/gitoxide PR #2886 ('fix: reject a lone @ as a reference name, like Git does', https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/pull/2886), merged 2026-08-06 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. A lone '@' is Git's shorthand for HEAD; Git refuses to create a reference literally named '@'. gix-validate accepted '@' as a valid partial reference name (name_partial returned Ok), and its sanitizing variant left '@' unchanged -- allowing a ref that collides with the HEAD shorthand (reference confusion / spoofing). The fix (gix-validate/src/reference.rs::validate) rejects a name that reduces to exactly '@' with the pre-existing Error::Reserved variant, and sanitizes it to '-', matching Git. This task slices the standalone gix-validate crate (restructured to a single crate at the repo root; edition 2024, rust-version 1.85, built on the :rust image which is rustc 1.87); its one dependency (bstr -> memchr) is vendored into repo/vendor with repo/.cargo/config.toml for offline runs. Hidden tests use the public reference:: API. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (751 source LOC; validate() still accepting a lone '@'; bstr and its vendored deps bring the tree to ~130k LOC, hence repo_scale xlarge); MIT/Apache-2.0 LICENSEs preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (name_partial('@') is now Err; sanitizing '@' yields '-'; sanitizing '//@//' -- which reduces to a lone '@' -- yields '-' not '@') plus a 2-check regression guard (an '@' inside a component like refs/heads/@ is still valid; an ordinary name is still valid).
